questions.question: What structures inside the cells of a plant leaf contain the machinery needed for photosynthesis?
options: Chloroplasts
Mitochondria
Vacuoles
Cell walls

questions.question: In which part of a plant cell does the process of photosynthesis actually take place?
options: In the nucleus
In the chloroplasts
In the cytoplasm
In the cell membrane

questions.question: What is the role of chlorophyll, the green substance found inside chloroplasts?
options: To absorb light energy for photosynthesis
To absorb water from the soil
To release carbon dioxide into the air
To store glucose as starch

questions.question: Why is it an advantage for plant leaves to be very thin?
options: It helps them float in water
It allows light to easily pass through to the cells containing chloroplasts
It prevents water from escaping the leaf
It makes it easier for roots to absorb minerals

questions.question: How does having a large surface area benefit a plant's leaves?
options: It helps the plant stand upright
It reduces the amount of water lost by evaporation
It allows the leaf to absorb more light for photosynthesis
It protects the leaf from being eaten by insects

questions.question: Which gas do plant leaves absorb directly from the air to use as a raw material in photosynthesis?
options: Oxygen
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Water vapour

questions.question: What happens to the oxygen gas that is produced during the process of photosynthesis?
options: It is released from the leaves into the air
It is stored in the roots as food
It is converted directly into minerals
It is completely used up to make chloroplasts

questions.question: What is the scientific term for the process where gases like carbon dioxide and oxygen enter and leave a plant leaf?
options: Transpiration
Gas exchange
Respiration
Fertilisation

questions.question: What are the tiny pores or holes on the surface of a leaf that allow gas exchange to happen called?
options: Capillaries
Stomata
Chloroplasts
Veins

questions.question: By which process do gas molecules move through the open stomata of a leaf?
options: Diffusion
Osmosis
Active transport
Suction

questions.question: Why are plants described as "producers" in an ecosystem?
options: They produce oxygen for themselves to breathe
They make their own food using photosynthesis
They produce soil from decaying matter
They consume other organisms for energy

questions.question: Under which of the following conditions is it possible for photosynthesis to take place in a plant?
options: Only when there is light
Only in complete darkness
Only during the winter season
At any time, regardless of light levels

questions.question: Which of these statements best describes the nature of photosynthesis?
options: It is a physical change that melts wax on the leaves
It is a single physical mixing process of gases
It is a series of chemical reactions that take place inside cells
It is a mechanical process carried out by the roots

questions.question: What are the chemical reactants and products of the photosynthesis process?
options: Reactants: oxygen and glucose; Products: water and carbon dioxide
Reactants: water and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and glucose
Reactants: minerals and nitrogen; Products: water and carbon dioxide
Reactants: glucose and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and water

questions.question: What does a word equation or word summary of photosynthesis represent?
options: A model of the overall chemical reactions of the process
A physical diagram of the leaf structures
A list of all the minerals absorbed by the roots
The exact speed at which gas exchange occurs

questions.question: Which of the following groups of resources must a plant have from its environment to stay alive and grow?
options: Light, air, water, and minerals
Light, soil, glucose, and oxygen gas only
Sugar, warmth, insects, and carbon dioxide
Water, oxygen, glucose, and darkness

questions.question: Through which parts of the plant are water and minerals absorbed?
options: Through the leaves
Through the flowers
Through the roots
Through the stem

questions.question: Which of the following is true about water and minerals for a plant?
options: They are the main food source absorbed by the plant
They are not food, but plants still need food to stay alive and grow
They replace the need for photosynthesis entirely
They are produced by the plant during the night

questions.question: How do plants obtain the food they need to survive?
options: They absorb dissolved food molecules from the soil
They trap and digest small insects through their roots
They do not take in food from their surroundings; they make it themselves
They feed on organic matter floating in the air

questions.question: What type of food do plants make during photosynthesis, and what is it used for?
options: They make minerals, which are used to absorb more water
They make carbohydrates, which they use for growth and as an energy source
They make proteins, which are used to attract pollinating insects
They make fats, which are stored to keep the leaves warm in winter
